book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 52 · Rescue Awareness and Operations
title: Rescue Scenes and Trapped Drivers: The PCP's Role
next: Chapter 52, Lesson 2: Confined spaces, trenches, water, rope and wilderness rescue

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already size up scenes, wear PPE, control bleeding, bind pelvises and restrict spinal motion. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Know the rescue training levels and the eight steps of a rescue
  2. Stay safe at a crash scene: traffic, power, airbags, glass
  3. Care for a patient trapped for a long time: IV, fluids, TXA, pain relief

Textbook: Chapter 52, PDF pages 4263–4312 (Introduction to Motor Vehicle Collisions)
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter 52, rescue. As EMRs, you've been to crash scenes: you size up the scene, wear PPE, control bleeding, bind a pelvis and restrict spinal motion. Rescue adds a new problem: the patient can't come to you. Freeing them may take a long time, and during that whole time the patient is yours. Today we'll cover three things. First, the levels of rescue training and the eight steps of every rescue. Second, staying safe around traffic, power lines, airbags and glass. Third, what you can now do as a PCP for a patient who's trapped for a long time.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第 52 章：救援。你们作为 EMR 都去过车祸现场：会评估现场、穿 PPE、止血、固定骨盆、限制脊柱活动。救援带来一个新问题：病人没法自己到你这里来。把他解救出来可能要很长时间，而这整段时间病人都归你管。今天讲三件事：第一，救援训练的级别和每次救援的八个步骤；第二，在车流、电线、气囊和玻璃周围怎样保证安全；第三，作为 PCP，对长时间被困的病人你现在能多做什么。

slides.title: Three levels of rescue training
slides.body:
Awarenessrecognize hazards, secure, call for helpno hands-on rescue; most paramedics
Operationshelp directly in the warm zonea limited part in the rescue
Techniciandoes the rescue itselfspecial tools, care, scene management

First rule of rescue: rescuer safety. Knowing your level keeps you out of rescues you aren't trained for.
slides.say: Rescue training has three levels. Awareness is the entry level: you recognize hazards, secure the scene and call for the right help, but you don't do the technical rescue. Operations level lets you work in the warm zone, right around the hazard, and help the rescue team in a limited way. Technicians do the rescue itself: special equipment, patient care during the rescue, and managing the scene. Most paramedic training is at the awareness level, yet your ambulance is often first to arrive, so your first decisions shape everyone's safety. Rescuer safety comes first, and knowing your level keeps you out of rescues you aren't trained for.
slides.sayZh: 救援训练分三个级别。认知级是入门级：识别危险、控制现场、呼叫合适的支援，但不实施技术救援。操作级可以在温区，也就是紧挨危险区的地方工作，有限度地协助救援队。技术员级亲自实施救援：使用专用装备、在救援过程中照护病人、管理现场。大多数院前急救人员的训练在认知级，可第一个到场的常常是你们的救护车，所以你最初的决定影响所有人的安全。救援者安全第一；清楚自己的级别，才能让你不去做没受过训练的救援。

slides.title: The eight steps of a rescue
slides.body:
Prepare→Respond→Arrive and assess→Stabilize
Access→Disentangle→Remove→Transport
  • Stabilize = control hazards, set zones, test the air
  • Life threats before disentangling, unless fire or explosion
  • Move before care only if a life is in immediate danger
slides.say: Every special rescue follows eight steps: preparation, response, arrival and assessment, stabilization, access, disentanglement, removal and transport. Preparation means training with fire and rescue teams before the call, so you know their tools and language. Stabilization is about the scene, not the patient: control hazards, set zones and test the air. Disentanglement means freeing the patient from whatever traps them. The key rule for you: unless there's an immediate threat like fire or explosion, do your primary survey and treat life threats before disentanglement starts: spinal motion restriction, airway, oxygen or ventilation, and major bleeding. Move a patient before that only when a life is in immediate danger.
slides.sayZh: 每次特殊救援都按八步走：准备、出动、到场评估、稳定、接近、解困、移出、转运。准备是指平时就和消防、救援队一起训练，熟悉他们的工具和术语。「稳定」针对的是现场而不是病人：控制危险、划分区域、检测空气。解困是把病人从困住他的东西里解脱出来。对你来说关键的一条：除非有火灾、爆炸这类即刻威胁，否则在解困开始前先做初步评估、处理危及生命的问题：脊柱活动限制、气道、给氧或通气、止大出血。只有在有人生命面临即刻危险时，才可以在这些处置完成前移动病人。

slides.title: Arriving: command, zones, accountability
slides.body:
• The first officer takes command and starts ICS
  • Zones: hot (red tape), warm (orange), cold (yellow)
  • Outer circle first: thrown patients, hazards, access routes
  • Inner circle: all the way round; look up and under
  • Accountability: who, where, doing what, on every call
slides.say: When you arrive, slow down and think. The first officer on scene takes command and starts the incident command system. Zones are often marked with tape: red for the hot zone around the hazard, orange for the warm zone, and yellow for the cold zone, where vehicles, equipment and the command post go. Do an outer circle survey first, looking for patients thrown from the vehicle, hazards, and ways in and out. Then an inner circle, all the way around, looking up for wires and underneath for people. And the accountability system, which tracks who is where doing what, is the most important process for rescuer safety, on every call.
slides.sayZh: 到场后先放慢节奏想一想。第一个到场的指挥官接管指挥、启动事故指挥系统。分区常用警戒带标出：红色是紧围危险点的热区，橙色是温区，黄色是冷区，车辆、装备和指挥所都放在冷区。先做外圈巡查，找被甩出车外的伤员、危险和进出路线；再做内圈巡查，绕一整圈，抬头看电线，低头看车底有没有人。人员追踪系统记录谁在哪里做什么，是保障救援者安全最重要的程序，每次出车都要用。

slides.title: Power lines and gas
slides.body:
Every downed wire is live

  • Park at least one truck length away, about 15 m
  • Wait for the power company; dark streetlights prove nothing
  • Fences, guardrails and water can carry current
  • Gas leak: call the gas company; the IC controls shut-off
  • Into gas only if trained, with SCBA and the IC's permission
slides.say: Utility hazards kill rescuers. Treat every downed wire as live until the power company has shut it off, and park at least one truck length away, about fifteen metres. Dark streetlights don't mean the wires are dead. Current can run along a metal fence or guardrail for its whole length, and through standing water. The BC Electrical Contact protocol agrees: don't approach until qualified personnel say it's safe. For a natural gas or propane leak, call the gas company and let the incident commander, the IC, control the shut-off. Only someone trained, in positive-pressure breathing apparatus and with the IC's permission, enters a gas-filled space.
slides.sayZh: 公用设施的危险会要救援者的命。所有断落的电线都当作带电，直到电力公司断电为止；车至少停在一个卡车车长以外，大约十五米。街灯灭了，不代表电线没电。电流能沿着金属围栏或护栏传遍全长，也能经积水传导。BC 的电击（Electrical Contact）流程也这样规定：在有资质的人员确认安全前不要靠近。遇到天然气或丙烷泄漏，通知燃气公司，由事故指挥官（IC）负责关断。只有受过训练、戴正压呼吸器、并经 IC 许可的人，才能进入充满燃气的空间。

slides.q: A car has hit a pole. A wire lies across the hood. The driver is awake with a bleeding scalp. The streetlights on the block are dark. What do you do?
options: Approach the car; the dark streetlights mean the power is off
Lift the wire off the hood with a dry wooden branch
Stay at least about 15 m back and wait for the power company
Reach the driver while touching only the rubber tires
slides.say: Time for a question. A car has hit a pole, and a wire lies across the hood. The driver is awake, with a bleeding scalp, and the streetlights on the block are dark. What do you do? A, approach the car, because the dark streetlights mean the power is off. B, lift the wire off the hood with a dry wooden branch. C, stay at least about fifteen metres back and wait for the power company. D, reach the driver while touching only the rubber tires. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道题。一辆车撞上电线杆，一根电线搭在引擎盖上。司机清醒，头皮在出血，这条街的街灯全灭了。你怎么做？A 走近车辆，街灯灭了说明已断电；B 用干树枝把电线从引擎盖上挑开；C 至少退到约十五米外，等电力公司来；D 只碰橡胶轮胎，伸手去够司机。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. Every downed wire is treated as live until the power company has de-energized it, and you stay at least one truck length, about fifteen metres, away. A is wrong because dark streetlights never prove a line is dead. B and D are improvised tricks that can kill you; the car and anything touching it may be energized. While you wait, talk to the driver from a safe distance and keep bystanders back.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。所有断落的电线都当作带电，直到电力公司断电；你要停在至少一个卡车车长、约十五米之外。A 错：街灯灭了永远不能证明电线没电。B 和 D 都是会要命的土办法：车辆和接触它的任何东西都可能带电。等待期间，在安全距离外和司机说话，把旁观者挡在外面。

slides.title: The crash scene: hidden hazards
slides.body:
• Traffic is the biggest single danger; angle a big unit as a shield
  • Only essential lights; headlights off; police run traffic
  • Undeployed airbags can still fire
  • Electric or hybrid: orange high-voltage cables; silent ≠ off
  • Propane or natural gas: leaks; use cones, not flares
  • Ethanol fire: bright blue, almost no smoke, hard to see by day
slides.say: At a highway crash, traffic is the biggest single danger. Park large vehicles at an angle as a shield, use only essential lights, turn off headlights, and let police run traffic. An airbag that didn't go off can still fire, even with the power disconnected. Electric and hybrid cars have high-voltage cables in orange insulation, and a silent car isn't necessarily switched off. Propane or natural gas vehicles can leak a lot of flammable gas, so use cones or triangles, not flares. And an ethanol fire burns bright blue with almost no smoke, so it's hard to see by day.
slides.sayZh: 高速公路车祸现场，最大的单一危险是车流。大型车辆斜着停作屏障，只开必要的警示灯，关掉前大灯，交通交给警察指挥。没弹出的气囊即使断了电也可能弹出。电动车和混动车的高压线包着橙色绝缘层，车子没声音不代表已经关闭。用丙烷或天然气的车辆可能漏出大量易燃气体，所以用锥桶或三角警示牌，不用照明弹。乙醇燃烧的火焰是亮蓝色、几乎没有烟，白天很难看见。

slides.title: Stabilize the car, then get in
slides.body:
1. Stabilize: cribbing at the wheels, step blocks under the sides
  2. Try every door first, even badly damaged ones
  3. Break a side or rear window (tempered), not the windshield
  4. Warn the patient, tape the glass, hit a lower corner
  5. Use the window farthest from the patient, unless care can't wait

Old rescue saying: try before you pry.
slides.say: Before anyone climbs in, the car must be stable. Cribbing, which means short blocks of hard wood, goes in front of and behind the wheels; step blocks go under the sides to stop the suspension moving; then the tires may be let down. Next, try every door, even ones that look ruined. If you must break glass, choose a side or rear window: that's tempered glass, which shatters into small pieces. The windshield is laminated and won't break that way. Warn the patient, tape the glass, hit a lower corner, and pick the window farthest from the patient, unless their condition can't wait.
slides.sayZh: 任何人钻进车之前，车必须先稳住。垫木就是一段段短的硬木块，塞在车轮前后；阶梯垫块塞在车身两侧下方，防止悬挂移动；然后可以给轮胎放气。接着，每扇门都先试一试，哪怕看起来已经坏了。如果必须破窗，选侧窗或后窗：那是钢化玻璃，会碎成小颗粒；挡风玻璃是夹层玻璃，这样打不碎。先警告病人，贴上胶带，敲下角，选离病人最远的那扇窗，除非病情等不了。

slides.title: Disentanglement: car off the patient
slides.body:
Remove the car from the patient, not the patient from the car

  • Seat moved back, windshield cut out, dash rolled, roof off
  • Cover the patient; protect eyes and ears; explain each noise
  • Undeployed airbag: nothing hard between it and the patient
  • Don't cut a steering wheel that holds an undeployed airbag
  • Stay out of the airbag's path; a deployed one is harmless
slides.say: The principle of disentanglement is simple: remove the car from around the patient, not the other way round. The team may move the seat back, cut out the windshield, roll the dashboard forward or take off the roof. Your job is protecting the patient: cover them with a blanket, shield their eyes and ears from glass and noise, and explain each loud step first. If an airbag didn't deploy, never put anything hard, like a backboard, between it and the patient, and don't cut a steering wheel with an undeployed airbag inside. Stay out of its path yourself. A deployed airbag is no longer a danger.
slides.sayZh: 解困的原则很简单：把车从病人身边拆走，而不是反过来。救援队可能把座椅后移、切下挡风玻璃、把仪表台向前推开，或拆掉车顶。你的任务是保护病人：盖上毯子，保护他的眼睛和耳朵免受玻璃和噪声伤害，每个响动大的步骤前先解释。如果气囊没弹出，绝不能在气囊和病人之间放任何硬物，比如背板；方向盘里有未弹出的气囊就不能切方向盘。你自己也要避开它弹出的路径。已经弹出的气囊就没有危险了。

slides.title: Caring for the trapped patient
slides.body:
• One provider stays with the patient throughout
  • Eye contact, the truth, simple words, Mr. or Ms. + last name
  • Keep them warm: you have a coat, they don't
  • Reassess ABCs and vital signs again and again
  • Stand by for injured rescuers too
slides.say: Once you're inside, one provider stays with the patient for the whole rescue. Talk to them: make eye contact, tell the truth, use simple words, and call them Mr. or Ms. with their last name. Explain each noise before it comes; a hydraulic tool beside your head is terrifying. Keep them warm. You're dressed for the weather and they aren't, and shivering makes pain worse. Reassess airway, breathing, circulation and vital signs throughout, because a patient who's stable at the start may not stay stable. And part of your job is standing by for the rescuers: if a crew member gets hurt, you're their paramedic too.
slides.sayZh: 进到车里后，要有一名急救人员在整个救援过程中一直陪着病人。和他说话：保持眼神接触，说真话，用简单的词，称呼「某先生」「某女士」加姓。每个响声来之前先解释；液压工具在耳边作响是很吓人的。给病人保暖：你穿着应对天气的衣服，他没有，而寒战会加重疼痛。全程反复评估气道、呼吸、循环和生命体征，因为开始时稳定的病人不一定一直稳定。你的任务还包括为救援人员待命：队员受伤了，你也是他们的急救员。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the trapped, bleeding patient
slides.body:
BC Hypovolemia protocol. PCP steps apply en route or with a time delay; a long extrication is a delay.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Control external bleeding
  • Splint pelvis / fractures if indicated
  • Supine when possible
  • Keep warm, prevent heat loss
  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%

PCP adds

  • Vascular access while still trapped
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • Consider TXA: 2 g IV over 1 minute
  • May start before BP falls if shock is expected
slides.say: The BC Hypovolemia protocol gives the PCP steps for en route or a time delay, and a long extrication is exactly that kind of delay. On the left, every level: control external bleeding, splint the pelvis or fractures if indicated, lay the patient flat when you can, keep them warm, and give oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher. On the right, the PCP adds vascular access while the patient is still trapped, a bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, and TXA, two grams IV over one minute, for shock from blood loss. You may even start before the pressure drops if shock is expected.
slides.sayZh: BC 低血容量流程规定 PCP 的措施在转运途中或「有时间延误」时执行，而长时间的破拆解救正是这种延误。左栏是各级别都做的：控制外出血，有指征时固定骨盆或骨折，能平卧就平卧，保暖，给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上。右栏是 PCP 多做的：病人还被困着就建立静脉通路；按每公斤二十毫升补液、最多两升、每五百毫升复评；失血性休克考虑 TXA，两克静脉推注、一分钟推完。如果预计会休克，甚至可以在血压下降前就启动。

slides.q: A driver is pinned by the dash. He was injured 2 hours 15 minutes ago; the crew needs about 45 more minutes. He is pale: HR 128, BP 84/56. As the PCP, what's best?
options: Wait to start the IV until he's in the ambulance
Start an IV now, bolus 20 mL/kg, and consider TXA
Give TXA at the hospital, where it's safer
Give ibuprofen for his pain and reassess
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A driver is pinned by the dashboard. He was injured two hours and fifteen minutes ago, and the crew needs about forty-five more minutes. He's pale, with a heart rate of one twenty-eight and a blood pressure of eighty-four over fifty-six. What's best? A, wait to start the IV until he's in the ambulance. B, start an IV now, give a bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram, and consider TXA. C, give TXA at the hospital, where it's safer. D, give ibuprofen for his pain and reassess. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名司机被仪表台压住，受伤已经两小时十五分钟，救援队还需要大约四十五分钟。他脸色苍白，心率一百二十八，血压八十四比五十六。最好的做法是什么？A 等他上了救护车再开静脉；B 现在就开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升补液，并考虑 TXA；C 到医院再给 TXA，更安全；D 给布洛芬止痛，然后复评。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The PCP steps in the BC Hypovolemia protocol apply during a time delay, and this extrication is one. TXA can't be given more than three hours after injury, and he'll still be trapped at that point, so it's now or never. A ignores both the delay and the shock. C misses the three-hour limit. D treats pain, not shock; pain relief comes after the life threat.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 低血容量流程中 PCP 的措施在有时间延误时就适用，这次破拆正是延误。TXA 在受伤超过三小时后不能给，而到那时他还被困着，所以要么现在给，要么就没机会了。A 既忽视了延误，也忽视了休克。C 错过了三小时的期限。D 治的是疼痛，不是休克；先处理危及生命的问题，再考虑止痛。

slides.title: Pain relief during a long rescue
slides.body:
• No drugs first: position, padding, gentle handling, talk, warmth
  • Entonox: not in a space you can't ventilate; not with altered LOC
  • Methoxyflurane 3 mL, repeat at 20 min, max 6 mL; stable adults
  • Acetaminophen or ibuprofen PO: check contraindications
  • IV acetaminophen 1,000 mg over 15 min (50 kg+) needs your IV

Book's morphine, fentanyl, ketamine, ketorolac: not on the BC exam (some are BCEHS added scope).
slides.say: Pain control matters in a long rescue; a patient in severe pain is hard to keep still. Start without drugs: position, padding, gentle handling, talk and warmth. On the BC licensing exam, the pain drugs are the same for EMRs and PCPs: Entonox, methoxyflurane, acetaminophen and ibuprofen. Entonox is out in a space you can't ventilate, or with altered consciousness or a possible pneumothorax. Methoxyflurane is three millilitres, repeatable after twenty minutes to a total of six, only for adults with a stable pulse and blood pressure and no head injury. What's new for you is the IV: IV acetaminophen, one gram over fifteen minutes for patients fifty kilograms or more, needs a line.
slides.sayZh: 长时间救援中镇痛很重要，剧痛的病人很难保持不动。先用非药物方法：体位、衬垫、轻柔搬动、聊天、保暖。在 BC 执照考试里，EMR 和 PCP 用的镇痛药是一样的：笑气（Entonox）、甲氧氟烷、对乙酰氨基酚和布洛芬。在无法通风的空间里、意识改变或可能有气胸时，不能用笑气。甲氧氟烷三毫升，二十分钟后可重复，总量最多六毫升，只用于脉搏和血压稳定、没有头部外伤的成人。你新增的是静脉通路：静脉对乙酰氨基酚，一克、十五分钟输完，适用于五十公斤以上的病人，需要一条静脉通路。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• The TXA clock keeps running while the patient is trapped
  • IV lines snag on metal and tools: secure them well
  • Check the patient and IV site every 5–15 minutes
  • Once free, the delay is over: go, do the rest en route
  • Entonox in a car: ventilation, chest injury, altered LOC
  • Reassess after every move: binder, splints, distal pulses
slides.say: Now the PCP watch-outs at a long extrication. The TXA clock keeps running while the patient is trapped, so decide early. Metal edges, tools and moving rescuers can pull out your IV line, so secure it well. BC's IV maintenance guideline says reassess the patient and the IV every five to fifteen minutes. Once the patient is free, the delay is over: move, and do the rest en route. Before Entonox, think about ventilation in the car, a possible chest injury, and the level of consciousness. And reassess after every move: the binder, splints and distal pulses can all change.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲长时间破拆时 PCP 要注意的事。病人被困期间，TXA 的时钟一直在走，要早做决定。金属边缘、工具和走动的救援人员都可能扯掉你的静脉管路，要固定好。BC 的静脉维护规定每五到十五分钟复评一次病人和静脉。病人一旦解脱，延误就结束了：马上走，其余的路上再做。用笑气前想清楚车里能不能通风、有没有可能的胸部外伤、意识水平如何。每次搬动后都要复评：骨盆带、夹板和远端脉搏都可能变化。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Hypovolemia: PCP steps en route or with a time delay
  • May start with systolic > 90 if shock is expected
  • TXA: not if > 3 h since injury, age < 12, or isolated head injury
  • Pelvis: commercial binder or 3 broad triangular bandages; no zap straps
  • Downed lines: don't approach until qualified personnel say safe
  • Opioids, ketamine, ketorolac: not on the exam (BCEHS added scope)
slides.say: For the BC exam: in the Hypovolemia protocol, the PCP steps happen en route or with a time delay, and the protocol may start with a systolic above ninety if shock is expected from the mechanism or the injuries. TXA is not given more than three hours after injury, under age twelve, or for an isolated head injury. Bind the pelvis with a commercial binder or three overlapping broad triangular bandages, never zap straps. Don't approach downed lines until qualified personnel say it's safe. And the book's opioids, ketamine and ketorolac aren't on the BC licensing exam, though BCEHS PCPs may give them after added-scope training.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要点：低血容量流程里，PCP 措施在转运途中或有时间延误时执行；如果受伤机制或伤情提示会出现休克，收缩压高于九十也可以启动这个流程。TXA 在受伤超过三小时、未满十二岁或单纯颅脑外伤时不能给。骨盆用商用骨盆带或三条重叠的宽三角巾固定，绝不能用扎带。在有资质的人员确认安全前不要靠近断落的电线。书里的阿片类药物、氯胺酮和酮咯酸都不在 BC 执照考试范围内，不过 BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1/2）培训后可以给。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Know your level: awareness means recognize, secure, call
  2. Scene first: wires are live, airbags can fire, try before you pry
  3. Trapped = time delay: PCP can start IV, fluids and TXA on scene

Next: confined spaces, trenches, water, rope and wilderness rescue
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: know your training level. At awareness level, you recognize hazards, secure the scene and call the right team. Two: the scene comes first. Every downed wire is live, undeployed airbags can fire, the car is stabilized, and you try the doors before anyone pries. Three: a trapped patient is a time delay, and that changes the PCP's plan. You can start the IV, give boluses and consider TXA before the patient is free. Next lesson: confined spaces, trenches, water and ice, rope and wilderness rescue. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，清楚自己的训练级别：认知级的任务是识别危险、控制现场、呼叫合适的队伍。二，现场安全第一：断落的电线一律带电，未弹出的气囊可能弹出，车要先稳住，先试门再撬。三，被困的病人就是「时间延误」，这会改变 PCP 的计划：病人解脱之前你就可以开静脉、补液、考虑 TXA。下节课讲密闭空间、沟渠、水域和冰面、绳索和野外救援。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
